narrative.northStar: The Window the Game Forgot to Ship
narrative.overview:
The overlay sits beside the game's own windows (the Quest Helper, the minimap) and is made from their materials: a translucent lavender-grey body, a steel-periwinkle title bar with a white top highlight and a dark-navy hairline, the map name in white bold lettering outlined in navy the way the minimap draws it, and the minimap's legend of blue portal rings and red mob dots. The game supplies the materials and one signature move. Organisation, hierarchy and density come from a working tool: hidden exits first, then the hunting numbers, then the credit. It is not a screenshot of a game window. The setup window and the title-marking window are built from the same materials, so every MapleCompass window reads as one more game window.

It is light because the game's windows are light, and dense because it is read in glances between attacks. Every state is drawn in the same window. Doubt and problems get the game's orange, and nothing else does. The confirmed rejection is the generic dark dev-tools card with a stats table on top, which this world replaced.

The overlay has no pointer interaction, so it has no hover or focus states. It is click-through except for dragging in edit mode, and its height follows its content. The setup window is clicked and tabbed through, so its buttons, and only they, carry hover, pressed, focus and disabled states. Nothing in any window moves: there is no motion.
keyCharacteristics: Light window body in the game's lavender (translucent over the game, opaque on the desktop), under a gradient steel-blue title bar.
Map name in outlined white lettering, with the Street Name above it as on the minimap.
Minimap glyphs (portal ring, mob dot) are the only icon vocabulary, drawn in CSS and SVG.
Game orange appears only for doubt and problems.
One plain bold sans (Arial) throughout; tabular figures in the overlay.
No hover or focus on the click-through overlay; interactive windows give their buttons the game's button states. No motion anywhere.

rules.name: The Orange Means Doubt Rule
rules.body: Game orange marks only uncertainty and problems: the "Not sure" chip, problem notes, the collapsed alert dot. A confirmed state never uses it, so orange can't become decoration.

rules.name: The Minimap Legend Rule
rules.body: Portal blue and mob red come from the minimap's legend and keep that meaning. Blue is for portals and red is for mobs, with no other uses.

rules.name: The Over the Game, Translucent Rule
rules.body: A window laid over the game uses the translucent Window Lavender (body); a window on the desktop uses the opaque one (body-solid). Same colour, different footing.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: In the overlay all figures are tabular (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on the body), and numeric columns are right-aligned so EXP, HP and share line up from one glance to the next.

rules.name: The Outlined Lettering Rule
rules.body: Only a Map Name uses white lettering with a navy outline (the shared `--lettering` text-shadow: a 1px stroke in eight directions plus one soft 0 2px 2px drop). It appears in the overlay title bar and in setup's recognised test read, nowhere else. Everything else is ink on the lavender body.

rules.name: The Notes Wrap, Names Truncate Rule
rules.body: Notes and the Map Name wrap so they can be read in full. Single-line facts (destinations, mob names, footer) truncate with an ellipsis instead of growing the panel.

rules.name: The Chrome, Not Lift Rule
rules.body: Depth is drawn the way the game draws it, with highlights and hairlines. Nothing floats on a blurred drop shadow.

dos: **Do** build new states and windows from the game's window materials: the Window Lavender body, the Title Bar Steel gradient with its white highlight and hairline, and navy ink.
